plugin.name: Jujutsu VCS Integration
plugin.description:
Native IntelliJ integration for Jujutsu (jj), a Git-compatible version control system with a fundamentally different approach to working with code.

Why Jujutsu?

Jujutsu treats your working copy as a commit—always. No staging area, no "dirty" state. Just describe what you're working on and keep coding.

Key Features

  • Describe-First Workflow — Working Copy tool window for describing current work and creating new changes.
  • Custom Log View — Visual commit graph with inline change IDs, descriptions, and bookmarks.
  • Change Operations — Edit, abandon, and describe changes directly from the log.
  • File History & Annotations — Full file history with diff viewer and line-by-line blame.
  • Multi-Repository Support — Work with multiple JJ repositories in a single project.
  • Real-Time Status — Auto-refresh keeps the UI in sync as you edit files.

GitHub · Issues
plugin.change-notes:
0.8.16

Added

  • Hovering a graph line whose other end (a distant ancestor/descendant, or a parent that hasn't loaded yet) is off-screen thickens the whole line and shows a directional cursor pointing toward it, plus a tooltip naming the target and how many rows up/down it is; if only one end is off-screen it always points there, and if both ends are off-screen which one it points to instead depends on which half of the visible log you're looking at. Clicking jumps there, loading it first if needed. A line hidden by the current filter shows the same tooltip but has no click action, since revealing it needs the filter cleared first.
  • In a colocated repo, the bookmarks panel no longer shows a `git` remote group alongside your real remotes — it was jj's own view of the colocated repo's local Git refs, not a peer remote, and made every bookmark appear a third time. Remote groups also now start collapsed by default (Local and Tags are unaffected), with expand/collapse persisted per log window; a collapsed group with an ahead/behind or untracked bookmark inside shows a roll-up indicator so you don't lose visibility into what's unsynced. New Expand All/Collapse All buttons in the panel's toolbar. ([#48](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/48), [#111](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/111))
  • Bookmark rows in the bookmarks panel now support the log's own change actions — New Change, New Change..., Edit Change, Rebase, and Duplicate — via right-click, including multi-select (Ctrl+Click several bookmark rows and "New Change From These" creates a merge with all of them as parents). Tag rows in the same panel gained the same actions. ([#48](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/48), [#108](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/108))
  • Every bookmark row action (Delete/Forget/Rename/Advance/Push to all remotes/Track/Untrack, plus Filter Log to Bookmark and Navigate Log to Bookmark) is now registered and keymap-assignable in Settings → Keymap, shows a shortcut hint in the bookmarks panel's own right-click menu once bound, and double-clicking a bookmark row navigates to its change the same way double-clicking a log row shows its diff. ([#48](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/48), [#109](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/109))
  • A local bookmark ahead of or behind its tracked remote now shows the same `↑n`/`↓m` divergence indicator on its own leaf in the bookmarks panel that a remote bookmark already showed — previously it always read 0/0 regardless of the actual state. With more than one tracked remote, the indicator shows the largest divergence rather than summing across remotes; per-remote detail is a follow-up. ([#48](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/48), [#110](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/110))
  • "Open Jujutsu Log" is now reachable from VCS → Jujutsu and from the VCS Operations popup, instead of only via Find Action or a manually-bound shortcut; invoking it while the log tab is already open but the tool window is hidden now brings it to the front instead of appearing to do nothing. ([#118](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/118))

    • Fixed

  • Splitting a change with zero whole files ticked but one or more files partially picked via "Pick Hunks…" was rejected with "Move at least one file to the child" — hunks-only splits (nothing fully ticked) now work as expected. ([#117](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/117))
  • The bookmarks panel always showed remote bookmarks with the "tracked" icon and never showed ahead/behind divergence, regardless of the actual state — an untracked remote bookmark's context menu also always offered "Untrack" instead of "Track". ([#48](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/48), [#110](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/110))
  • A conflicted or divergent local bookmark (e.g. moved to different targets by two concurrent operations) vanished from the bookmarks panel entirely, even though the log table still showed it with its conflict marker — the same defect affected conflicted tags. ([#110](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/110))
  • A stale jj workspace (`jj workspace update-stale`) no longer breaks the Working Copy tool window, or shows a wrong/missing message instead of the right one — this now covers essentially every command and dialog, not just the Working Copy panel: Advance/Rename/Create/Move Bookmark, Set Tag, Push, Show History, and the Split/Squash/Rebase/New Change dialogs' commit pickers. All now offer a one-click "Update Stale Workspace" action that repairs it and automatically finishes whatever you were doing. (Annotate still reports the error as before — a fix attempt there didn't pan out.)
  • Renaming or creating a bookmark could show a flatly wrong "There is already a bookmark with that name" error for any failure at all (e.g. an invalid target revision) — it now only shows that message when jj actually reports a name conflict.
  • The Move Bookmark dialog could warn that a move was "backward or sideways" even when it was genuinely forward, if the classification query failed for any reason (including a stale workspace) — it now surfaces the failure instead of silently guessing backward.
  • A large changes tree with a Jujutsu repository root visible could freeze the UI for tens of seconds — the repo-root icon lookup was doing a blocking VCS-root resolution from inside the tree's paint path on every repaint.
  • A commit whose parent has been filtered out of view now shows a wiggly line down from its circle instead of no connector at all — which looked identical to a true repository root.
  • A commit whose parent falls beyond the configured log limit now shows a faded straight line down from its circle instead of no connector at all — which looked identical to a true repository root. A commit whose parent has been filtered out of view instead shows a wiggly line, since that's genuine elision (like jj's own `~`) rather than history that simply hasn't loaded yet — the two previously looked the same. A merge with one loaded parent and one unresolved parent now shows its stub too, in its own lane alongside the real connector.
  • Settings → Keymap showed the raw action id instead of a real name for the main-toolbar bookmark widget (`Jujutsu.MainToolbarBookmarks`) and "Undo Last Jujutsu Operation" (`Jujutsu.UndoLastOperation`).
  • Settings → Version Control → Jujutsu's "Installation Help" no longer goes stale while Settings stays open: clicking Test now previews its wording, gated-feature list, and command rows against the path you just tested — even before clicking Apply — instead of only updating after reopening Settings. A fully up-to-date jj also now shows neutral "how to update later" wording and update commands, instead of "if jj is not installed, use...".
  • Installation Help's Cargo upgrade command now passes `--force`, instead of being identical to the install command — without it, `cargo install` refuses to overwrite an already-installed `jj` binary, so the shown command would have failed instead of upgrading.
  • Every mutating command (New Change, Edit, Abandon, Rebase, Squash, Split, Duplicate Onto, Restore, Undo, resolving a merge conflict, switching working copies) could briefly freeze the UI on a large repository, tripping IntelliJ's "slow operation may freeze UI" assertion — the post-command VFS refresh's recursive directory walk ran synchronously on the EDT despite requesting an async refresh; it now runs on a background thread. ([#113](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/113))
  • On IntelliJ IDEA 2025.1, running any jj command could crash with "Access is allowed from write thread only" — the pre-command document-save check queried whether writing was allowed before acquiring the write-intent lock that check itself required on that platform version.
  • Resolving a rebase conflict could show your own change as "Theirs" and the commit you rebased onto as "Yours" — which side jj renders as full content vs. a diff varies per conflict, not per operation, so a fixed guess was right about half the time. The merge tool now reads jj's own per-side label from the conflict markers and names the panes after the actual commits (falling back to "Side #1"/"Side #2" when markers carry no commit info), and orients "Yours" to your own change; merge and squash conflicts are unaffected. ([#112](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/112))
  • Double-clicking a conflicted file's diff for any commit other than the working copy showed "Cannot show diff: Could not extract conflict data" (or, worse, silently showed the working copy's unrelated conflict) — the diff always read the file from disk regardless of which commit's diff was opened. It now reads that commit's own conflicted content, so browsing the log to a conflicted commit shows its own three-way conflict, whether it's an ancestor of the working copy, a descendant that inherited the conflict, or an unrelated commit. ([#119](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/119))
  • The log graph got measurably slower to repaint and to hover the further down a long log you scrolled — drawing a row's connector lines rescanned every row above it, and hovering a long edge rebuilt its whole lane index on every mouse move and scroll tick instead of reusing the cache already built for it. Both now do constant work per row/event regardless of scroll position or log size.

    • See full release notes for details.
